Bespreking van studente 1
De zuster had de eerste keer dat zij de opdracht gemaakt had, die desondanks op een niet helemaal juiste wijze gedaan. Het beeld dat de zuster over haar ouders had wat betreft hun positie tegenover haar, was niet helemaal juist.
Zij koos de eigenschap van al-hilm en al-anaah. Dat betekent geduld gepaard met het gebruik van behoedzaamheid en verstand. Zij ging er nog niet op de juiste wijze mee om en zij wilde proberen daar verandering in te brengen.
En daarnaast koos zij dat de vermaning niet voortdurend is. Er dient tussen de verschillende vermaningen een tijdsruimte te zijn zodat de mens niet verveeld raakt. Er dient meer kwaliteit dan kwantiteit te zijn. Hiermee hield de zuster zich bewust bezig. Zij is in haar omgeving met een bekeerde zuster die ongeveer drie jaar geleden moslim geworden is; zij merkt ook aan haar, in haar manieren en haar gedrag, dat zij daar veel in tekortschiet en dat veel van haar oude opvoeding, dat hele Nederlandse karakter, nog in haar zit. Zij probeert haar te adviseren om kennis te vergaren. Een tijdlang was dat bij de bekeerde zuster vervelend als zij ook maar iets kleins ter herinnering zei. Nu hield de zuster zich daar op een andere wijze mee bezig. Zij koos ervoor een tijdsruimte te laten, maar op een andere wijze. Bijvoorbeeld: binnenkort begint er een cursus voor bekeerlingen en geïnteresseerden. «Als je wilt, kun je je ook inschrijven, wij kunnen samen met de auto gaan, je leert veel meer mensen kennen», enzovoort. De zuster merkt dat [de zaak] dan beter valt, hoewel de zuster zegt dat zij geen tijd heeft en/of dat zij moet werken, maar zonder dat er vijandigheid [is]. De zuster ziet dat als een stap dichter bij het vergaren van kennis.
En daarnaast koos zij ervoor een goed voorbeeld te zijn. Om Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa niet ongehoorzaam te zijn. Dat was ook met een zuster die zij goed kent. Zij zaten samen in de auto en gingen naar de les, maar zij waren een beetje moe. Zo begon hun gesprek ook dat zij niet goed geslapen hadden en dergelijke zaken. Toen zei de zuster: nee, wij zullen vandaag niet negatief zijn maar wij zullen vandaag positief zijn. In plaats van op te sommen hoe moe zij waren, [gingen zij] de gunsten noemen, dat zij desondanks toch een beetje hadden kunnen slapen, en dat zij de lessen zouden vervolgen, en dat zij de shaytaan hadden overwonnen. Op een bepaald moment ging de andere zuster daarin mee totdat zij beiden positieve zaken bevestigden.
Er is [tussen haar] en die zusters geen opvoedkundige band, maar het zijn zaken die zij aanhaalde wat betreft de opdracht en wat zij ermee gedaan heeft.
Bespreking van studente 2
Zij behandelde de tweede eigenschap (de zorgzaamheid en de zachtheid). Zij kan niet goed onderscheid maken tussen de fitrah-eigenschappen [en de persoonlijkheidseigenschappen], en zij vraagt of de zorgzaamheid tot de fitrah-eigenschappen behoort.
De leraar: De zorgzaamheid behoort niet tot de fitrah-eigenschappen maar is iets dat jij verwerft.
De zuster: In de zachtheid overdrijft de zuster soms, zodat het haar moeilijk valt om grenzen te stellen aan anderen. Zij neigt er snel toe te denken «het is maar een kind», bijvoorbeeld bij diefstal. Dat is een valkuil waarin zij voortdurend betrapt wordt.
De leraar: Dat is geen overdrijving in de zachtheid, dat is een vorm van het verwaarlozen van de verantwoordelijkheid. Het probleem is dat wanneer je het onder de zachtheid schaart, je het niet zult oplossen, je het niet zult corrigeren, maar juist het tegenovergestelde van het gewenste zult doen, zodat je harder wordt en denkt dat je het kunt oplossen. Wanneer je het onder de juiste benaming schaart (de verwaarlozing), dan zul je alerter zijn in je gevoel. Wanneer je kind zoiets doet, als het groot/tiener zou zijn, welk oordeel zou een dergelijk gedrag krijgen (zonde, geen zonde, grote zonde), overeenkomstig dat oordeel dien je je opvoedkundig te gedragen, want de opvoeding van het kind is een voorbereiding op zijn buloegh, zodat het voorbereid wordt om zijn verantwoordelijkheid te dragen wat betreft zijn daden en woorden. Dat betekent dat haar gevoel wat betreft zijn daad of woord niet geringschattend of nalatig mag zijn. De trouw aan Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa dient goed te zijn in zulke mate dat je de daad ook behandelt overeenkomstig het oordeel van de daad.
Een voorbeeld daarvan is dat een kind — bijvoorbeeld — snoep pakt zonder toestemming. Als het wat ouder zou zijn, zou dat diefstal genoemd worden. Zo dien je het in je hart te noemen. Een kind dat een ouder slaat, zou een grote zonde zijn als het opgroeit. Een kind dat niet de waarheid spreekt en er een grap van maakt, hoe zou dat genoemd worden als het opgroeit, enzovoort.
Daarmee bereid je hem voor, anders is die [persoon] zo achteloos dat hij in werkelijkheid een roddelaar, een dief, een bedrieger, een leugenaar opvoedt, onder het mom van de troost «ach, het is nog klein».
De Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam zat met 3abdullaah ibn 3abbaas [3umar ibn Abie Salamah] aan tafel en zag zijn hand rondgaan in de schotel. Toen zei hij tegen hem: «يا غُلام، سَمِّ الله، وكُل بيمينك، وكُل مما يَليك»[^18]. («O jongen, noem de Naam van Allaah, en eet met je rechterhand, en eet van wat vlak voor je is».) Als [de zaak] verband houdt met dergelijke gedragsmanieren die verplicht zijn, dan is het laten van deze zaken klein. Maar wat betreft de grote zonden, dan dien je hem daarop nog meer te wijzen en hem die te doen verafschuwen.
Het kind, daarmee vorm je zijn 3aqiedah. Wat betekent de 3aqiedah precies? Sommige mensen denken direct aan de Tawhied van de aanbiddingswaardigheid (uloehiyyah), de namen en eigenschappen, en het heerschap (ruboebiyyah), maar dat is niet volledig. Jij vormt zijn liefde en zijn haat en de wijze waarop hij liefheeft en haat. Jij bepaalt voor hem de bron, wat hij dient lief te hebben en hoe hij dat dient te doen, en wat hij dient te haten en hoe hij dat doet. Dat [is] de kern van de 3aqiedah waarmee hij zich beweegt.
Als je dat niet doet [is het] als troost voor jezelf of achteloosheid. Als je dat niet doet, dan geef je een averechtse opvoeding.
Wanneer je het probleem verbindt aan een onjuiste oorzaak, dan zul je de oplossing niet vinden en zul je het probleem vergroten of juist een extra probleem toevoegen.
De zuster: Bij de vierde eigenschap (het beheersen van de woede) betrapte de zuster zichzelf erop dat zij, wanneer zij boos wordt, boos wordt om persoonlijke zaken en niet om waar Allaah of de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam boos om wordt.
De leraar: Hoe heb je dat verbeterd?
De zuster: Bij de woede keek ik of Allaah hier boos om wordt.
De leraar: Kun je hier een voorbeeld van geven?
De zuster: Meer persoonlijke ergernissen vanwege — bijvoorbeeld — een geërgerd gezicht. Meer ergernissen wekken mijn woede op. Zij kalmeert zichzelf door te weten waarom ik hier boos om word, wat zijn mijn prioriteiten? Stel dat een islamitische zaak geschonden wordt, dan neigt de zuster ertoe een excuus te zoeken voor die [persoon].
Voorbeeld: stel dat iemand geen hoofddoek draagt: zij probeert excuses te verzinnen waarom de zuster geen hoofddoek draagt. En zij overdrijft daarin in zulke mate dat zij het als een kleinere zaak ziet.
Dat houdt verband met de woede, omdat zij de woede niet in het hart wil bewaren, terwijl zij in werkelijkheid de woede in haar hart zou dienen te willen bewaren, maar zij probeert zichzelf te kalmeren. Haar weegschaal is volgens de zuster niet juist.
De leraar: Dit is geen goede veronderstelling, [noch] een goede beredenering of [de zaak] juist is of niet. In werkelijkheid dien je jezelf af te vragen: geef ik er de voorkeur aan haar te adviseren of niet? Is [de zaak] dat ik een grote belemmering ervaar om te adviseren, of is er iets anders?
De zuster: Misschien is de eerste zaak dat ik daarin overdrijf, zodat zij haar verantwoordelijkheid om advies te geven verwaarloost.
De leraar: Jouw metgezel (je gezel [van de djinn]) kent jouw begeerten en laat je jezelf troosten zodat je niet overgaat tot het advies. Ook dit is geen goede veronderstelling. Het juiste is dat je denkt «deze zuster zou graag geadviseerd worden en ik zal haar adviseren om haar af te wenden van het Vuur en de vervloeking waarin zij zich bevindt». Een goede veronderstelling is alleen iets dat je dichter bij het welbehagen van Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa brengt, niet iets dat je verwijdert van het welbehagen van Allaah.
Wanneer je allerlei excuses gaat verzinnen om het niet-dragen van de hoofddoek te rechtvaardigen of [ermee] te troosten, dan betekent dat in werkelijkheid dat je zegt dat Allaah haar daar niet op voorbereid heeft, dat zij niet weet of zij de hoofddoek draagt, [dat] als ik haar adviseer, zij bozer zal worden.
Wie heeft bevolen dat er geadviseerd wordt? Allaah. En Hij is Degene wiens hart in Zijn hand is.
De goede veronderstelling over de mensen is gebouwd op de goede veronderstelling over Allaah en hangt daarvan af en is daarnaar. Dan weet je dat Allaah je zal leiden, en jij doet dit met de kennis die je gekregen hebt, Allaah zal je helpen, die zekerheid heb je. Deze goede veronderstelling over Allaah zal je ertoe leiden te denken dat haar hart in de hand van Allaah is wanneer Hij weet dat zij het goede wil.
De goede veronderstelling over de mensen hangt af van de goede veronderstelling over Allaah en is daarmee verbonden. Dit mag nooit vergeten worden. Het is jou nooit ofte nimmer toegestaan een zonde gering te achten, of die te verwaarlozen, of die te laten [voortbestaan].
De zonden behandel je overeenkomstig de wijze van de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam; soms leert hij ons om direct te handelen, en soms om te confronteren, dat is overeenkomstig de situatie.
Wij hebben ook eerder de methoden van de vermaning behandeld. En wij hebben ook eerder de adviezen behandeld, wanneer je een openlijk advies geeft, en een privéadvies, wanneer [het] op de bedekking [is], je hebt meerdere vormen van de bedekking.
De Sunnah leert ons hoe wij daarmee dienen om te gaan, niet onze begeerten. Als je een fout maakt in de inschatting van de Sunnah, dan is dat beter dan dat je denkt dat je het goed gedaan hebt. Een fout op een goede grondslag is beter dan een goede daad gebouwd op een slechte grondslag. De goede daad gebouwd op een slechte grondslag is in ieder geval slecht.
Krijg je een beloning voor de gedachten die op je begeerten gebouwd zijn? Nee. Ook al zou je overeenkomstig de Sunnah op een goede wijze handelen. Maar wanneer je gedachten op je begeerten gebouwd waren, dan krijg je geen beloning en heb je niet gedaan wat Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa behaagt.
Wanneer je overweging de Sunnah is, dan zul je op dat moment, ondanks dat je een fout hebt gemaakt, voor je fout een beloning krijgen, omdat je gewedijverd hebt om het goede te verkrijgen, om de Sunnah te volgen.
Bij de geleerden van de metgezellen noemden zij [de zaak] pas fiqh [begrip] wanneer die persoon de kennis ook in de praktijk brengt. De mens heeft pas fiqh wanneer zij weten hoe zij die in de praktijk dienen uit te voeren. Daarom hebben sommigen van hen meer kennis dan anderen, want die [persoon] brengt met minder informatie ten minste die kennis in de praktijk, en wie meer kennis heeft [maar] de kennis niet in de praktijk brengt, heeft dus minder kennis.
De zuster: De zevende eigenschap (het leren wat de gematigdheid is) heeft de zuster nog, maar zij had die in de vorige les behandeld.
Bespreking van studente 3
sections.title_nl: 9. Dat [de mens] een goed voorbeeld is en het gebod van Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa niet ongehoorzaam is
sections.content_en:
The teacher had taught us that Allaah does not love that we say what we do not do.
Question: Is it correct that the [not] saying of what you do not do also applies to the (announcing of) the sin?
The teacher: The sins that are known anyway or can be known to the people (everyone knows whether you pray or do not pray), that you say «no, I do not want to announce my sin».
By leaving the prayer and not wearing the headscarf, you have already announced your sins. Some sins are themselves an open committing of the sin. For example the backbiting: if someone backbites, that is an open sin. There are sins that the person can commit while he covers himself in them (for example that he smokes but in the presence of the people does not smoke and in secret smokes, or that he watches bad films or images), then [the matter] is a sin. When you cover yourself in it (if you do it when you are alone), then you should keep yourself covered. The sins that you commit without anyone knowing about them, you should cover. And the sins that you commit openly, thereby you have already disgraced yourself.
Discussion of student 3
Al-hilm and al-anaah: [in] a certain educational bond with the children of her brothers and sisters she sees that she gets a certain behaviour [in return] and that the result that she wants to reach is not realised. When she takes an overarching perspective [from above] (does not go along with the behaviour and guards the results) she notices that the results are much better. That overlaps with the fourth point: if they become angry, that she [then] becomes angry and goes along in that, but if she calms herself and indicates in a strict but calm tone that they should not do that, she sees an improvement.
The sister thinks that this is so because they need structure [a system] and need opposite [contrary] behaviour.
The teacher: It does not necessarily have to be opposite behaviour, [the matter] is that you as an educator hold the steering wheel in your hand, that you can drive yourself and thereby can drive him.
And it is also intended that you are above the behaviour and that you also radiate that: I will not go along with you, I see that what you do leads you to misery, so I will try to correct you.
It is among the fitrah of the human being that the child (or the person who is brought up), when it sees that the educator weakens (that he goes along in the feelings or surrenders himself to his feeling), that it [then] will misuse this weak position.
And besides that it is also important that you know that every human being, every person, needs authority. However high this person is. Therefore Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «ولولا دَفعُ الله الناسَ بعضَهم ببعضٍ لفَسَدَتِ الأرض». («And were it not for Allaah repelling the people, some by means of others, the earth would become corrupted».)
The explanation:
That means that both the child and the parent need authority and both need a counter-pole, because when that counter-pole is not there, a successive trajectory of annoyance and evil etc. arises. That counter-pole should be present in order to restrain the other. Authority every person needs. Some children crave negative behaviour.
The child, that you can see more in its behaviour than you can hear it in its words. In reality its fitrah needs authority. We should, besides the person himself, also communicate with the fitrah of the human being, because if you know the fitrah of the human being, you also know how the human being is driven and what the human being needs. And if it is known what he needs, not everyone will be honest in that or show it.
This is an essential matter. To keep your upbringing very pure, speak with the fitrah of the human being. In his fitrah every human being needs authority. Sometimes it radiates that he is rebellious, then you should go looking for the correct key person who can have authority over him. Sometimes [the matter] is not a person but a deed, and sometimes it can be a person.
A simple example of that which the teacher knows is that with many women [the matter] is that when they need attention, it no longer matters to them what attention it is, even if it is negative attention. Some people have [in] a psychological [need] for attention to such an extent that, [even if] the attention is coupled with violence, they enjoy it because they are looking for attention and crave authority.
Sometimes [the matter] is that she, instead of saying to the man «I love you, I long for you», goes and provokes problems with him.
Often [the matter] is that in the characteristic of the fitrah of the human being (this we dealt with before when we dealt with the different characteristics of the fitrah). Different fitrah characteristics together can form a certain character.
The human being is in his core social. We have here the characteristic that he is a social being, but the human being also loves much the good for himself.
A third fitrah characteristic is that the human being also loves fame, recognition, and publicity.
And another fitrah characteristic is that the human being also loves immortality.
Which fitrah characteristics do we have now here?
A social being
The good for himself
Fame, recognition, and publicity
Immortality
Look well at these four characteristics. According to what drives them therein (the heart is driven by the fitrah characteristics, the experience, and the 3aqiedah. According to the 3aqiedah (the most important thing that drives the heart), whether it is of disbelief or of Islam, according to that the personality is formed and the person has faith or not).
So here — for example — an incorrect 3aqiedah drives her fitrah in the four characteristics that we have mentioned. That means that the miserliness will here too play a very great role. But built on worldly matters more than on matters of the hereafter. All of this (that he is social, and the good for himself, and the fame/recognition, and the immortality, and the miserliness) leads to the person being either loud or very silent, but in both cases they have almost one personality characteristic, namely that they love attention.
The person can also be very silent (according to his personality characteristics; some are active and some passive). The active person will lean more towards loudness, and the passive person will lean more towards silence. In both cases they can [agree on] the same thing, namely that they are looking for attention, and in a wrong way and with wrong intentions.
The silent one will be more cunning, and the loud one will be more violent.
So you see that not every silent one is a sensible person and not every loud one is an unsensible person. There are silent people who are cunning and do evil and thereby also attract attention, because the people around them are louder, so they attract the attention with their silence, and they will react to the people in a way that differs from the loud one.
This is a short, quick analysis driven by an incorrect 3aqiedah.
When the fitrah characteristics are driven by a correct 3aqiedah, then they do not use these characteristics to attract attention but to please Allaah. Naturally that will swing back and forth between the obligatory and the recommended faith (sometimes the person has more faith than at other moments), but the general line remains towards the pleasure of Allaah. That means that his fitrah characteristics/skills, that he drives himself towards the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
Here you see that we should communicate more, and take into account the fitrah characteristics alongside the individual personality. You have — for example — people who are very silent, but in their hearts volcanoes are working, but in a silent, cunning way. And you have people who are silent as the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam speaks about them (the believer) who is [like] the noble inexperienced one. The noble inexperienced one is the one who appears as an inexperienced one [with little experience] but is noble. His nobility comes from the fact that he can cause the people harm but does not do it.
And the disbeliever is, as the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam says, miserly and cunning in a hideous way.
What is the difference? The faith, the 3aqiedah (believer, disbeliever).
What the teacher just said about the fitrah characteristics (the personality changes according to the 3aqiedah, but the fitrah characteristics remain as they are), the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam also said.
We as educators should place ourselves above the behaviour of the one we bring up. This is not arrogance, because thereby you do not go and belittle the people. In order to preserve the analytical capacity, it is important that you place yourself above the behaviour of the one you bring up. Whether it is negative or positive, in both cases you should place yourself above it, then you drive, but if you descend, then it is your feeling that drives and there is no upbringing anymore.
----------------------------------- Questions ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Question 1:
Does every human being have the fitrah characteristics in himself and do they develop according to the 3aqiedah that you follow, or does every human being have different kinds of fitrah characteristics?
The answer: Every human being has the same bodily fitrah characteristics. And you also have the psychological fitrah characteristics. You should distinguish between the innate [inherited] fitrah characteristics and the personality characteristics. The personality characteristics depend on the driving [the steering], the experience, the 3aqiedah, and the quality of these fitrah characteristics. All of that forms a personality.
For example: is your hand as strong as the hand of another sister? In that there is a difference. You do with your hand [something] that differs from what other sisters do. The fitrah characteristics [are] with everyone, but the quality and the quantity with which we use them differ.
Every person is forgetful. That means that this is a fitrah characteristic. But not everyone is heedless [neglectful]. About what are we heedless? When are we heedless about something? Heedlessness is the conscious neglect of what we should do. We do this when we consider the importance of something small. When we love [something] less, we consider [something else more important]. When we see no benefit in it, we consider its importance small. The 3aqiedah determines whether we see benefit in it or not.
The difference is that we do the one consciously and the other we carry out unconsciously. When we forget something, we should Islamically say «I was made to forget it» [it was made forgotten to me]. The shaytaan makes us forget the good. The young man who went looking for al-Khadir said: «وما أَنسانيهُ إلَّا الشيطان». («And none but the shaytaan made me forget it».) So from now on we do not say «I forgot it» but we say «it was made forgotten to me».
When we consider something important [see it as important], we will focus on it completely. Then we cannot forget it. The only thing possible is that someone (the shaytaan) makes us forget it, but we cannot forget it [from ourselves], because we see it as important.
What happens now is that the person often takes the fitrah characteristics as an excuse, whereas [the matter] is in reality heedlessness about the personality characteristics.
Everyone has forgetfulness, but not everyone deals with the forgetfulness like the other, and not everyone has the same quantity as the others.
------------------------------- The end of the questions --------------------------------------------------------------------------
The teacher asks: «How can we put this knowledge into practice?»
We should look at the child by first addressing the fitrah characteristics, because that forms the 3aqiedah. The upbringing plays a very great role in the upbringing of the child. The fitrah characteristics you should form so that they become a personality characteristic, so you should form the personality characteristics. When you form a personality characteristic, you should as a mother be very aware of it but also drive it, so you should also know how you drive it, such as that you do not go and command before you convince of the benefit or the harm in it. And before you can convince someone, you should enter his heart. Before you can move someone or change something in his heart, his heart should be in your hand. This we also dealt with during [the talk about] the communication between man and woman. If you want Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa to do for you everything that pleases Allaah, then take his heart in your hand, then you can obtain from him what he wants [drive him to where he should]. And the same with the woman: ensure that you drive her in a sincere, just way of trust towards the pleasure of Allaah.
If you cannot enter the heart and the heart is not in your hand, then you will only be able to do little or nothing, and you will have rebellion, wars, and misery.
-------------------------------------------------------------------- Questions -------------------------------------------------------
Question 1:
Is the aggression a fitrah characteristic in every human being and is it formed by the 3aqiedah? Someone who — for example — is by nature very aggressive, is he born that way?
The answer: The aggression is not a fitrah characteristic but a personality characteristic. And such a personality characteristic can be positive or negative. War is aggression. The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam waged war. The aggression is formed by one of the fitrah characteristics of the human being; one of the fitrah characteristics is that he always defends himself, that he wants to defend himself in order to remain, and another fitrah characteristic is that he is stubborn. And another characteristic is that he denies (the denial). All these characteristics and other characteristics together — and you should not see the human being as one fitrah characteristic but as an integrated, coherent structure of fitrah characteristics that complement one another — will, according to his 3aqiedah, drive his fitrah characteristic towards the negative or towards the positive.
Question 2:
Two sisters teach. The sister notices that the behaviour (that you are above the matter) is sometimes hard for her because she knows the other sisters. The rule is that everyone should be present beforehand, and that the two teachers sometimes come late and the students wait. Then they point to their watches and look at the clock. Sometimes the lesson begins at nine o'clock, then they come at nine o'clock and say: «You must have been very tired; we always have to come on time and now you yourselves are late». The sisters are older than they or of their age. How can we be better in this?
The answer: The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam had an educational task. And the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam as an educator was not always the oldest of the people. That means that he dealt with those who were older, such as his uncles for example, [or] such as Ibn 3abbaas, who was older than him or of his age. That means that an older or younger person can also bring up an older person, but then it is important that he has more knowledge, and gives the correct example, and besides that is very patient in his behaviour. These are three characteristics:
That he has more knowledge
That he gives the correct example
That he is very patient
These three characteristics give authority over whoever is older than them in age. Without these characteristics his authority will be absent. When he has less knowledge and does not give the correct example and is not patient in his behaviour, then he no longer has authority. And the more he loses of these characteristics, the less his authority becomes.
The authority is not everything. The authority is present, and the softness should also be present. And especially when you deal with older sisters who have not yet been brought up as you have been brought up (the gathering of knowledge, that they be brought up again), but they are sisters who are in general in a good state, but they want a certain knowledge that you have and they do not, this causes that the relationship teacher/student and student/teacher is sometimes not optimal and sometimes clashes in that.
When you return to these three characteristics (the knowledge, the example, and the patience) and elevate yourself above this behaviour by giving the correct example and transferring the knowledge in the correct way and being patient with such behaviour, then you will improve such behaviour and you will have more authority, because they will reduce such statements. And it can also be that they keep performing such behaviour, that means that you should have more patience with that. That will enlarge your authority.
Why do you need that authority?
To transfer the knowledge for the sake of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. That last thing (the sincerity) should drive all these characteristics. The sincerity should drive the knowledge and the good example and the patience. Then you will also notice that no annoyance about that comes into your heart. Thus you drive yourself.
If you come late and they look at their watches, then you should the next time give a good example, and if you have no patience with that, your influence will decrease, therefore you should beware of that. If you cannot always be the correct example 100%, you should drive yourself with patience, so that you can transfer the knowledge.
Example: someone who leads a group. A young man of thirty years who leads a group of people who are all older than him. He has more knowledge than them and cannot always give the best example. Sometimes forgetfulness distracts him, sometimes he is very busy (so he says at least), but he has authority over these people.
The more you acknowledge the mistakes with those you lead, the more these people take you seriously and the more authority you have. That differs from what many people think: «If I acknowledge my mistake, I will have no authority», no, that is the thought of the shaytaan. The people will then have no awe for you and will no longer give you authority if you do not acknowledge your mistake.
When you enter there, you say: «Correct, I am late, I apologise, o noble sisters, but if I make a mistake, that does not mean that you should make a mistake. Thus we should remind one another to do the best for the sake of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa».
When you feel that annoyance in your heart, if you reconsider it well and deeply, is it because Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa is displeased with that, or because you feel that you have been personally attacked?
Is Allaah displeased with their behaviour, or do you find it difficult at that moment because you have been personally addressed? Does [the matter] feel personal, or is it because Allaah is displeased, and that they have committed a sin, so therefore [you are angry].
You should place yourself above the personal [the subjective].
The sister: In the past the sister laughed along with them, and they also study Arabic with a teacher regarding how you should teach, and she says that we should not go along with the behaviour of the students, because it is Islamically incorrect. You should show much awe towards the one who teaches, so then the sister no longer laughed along with them when they did that. She is [in] a different position. Precisely during the teaching she is aware of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and considers herself unworthy to stand before the class, so she is consciously engaged with that, so [that] was according to her for the sake of Allaah that she felt that annoyance.
The teacher: If it is for the sake of Allaah, then it is important that you also make clear to them how they should behave, not by saying «you behave badly, you do wrong», but give them a story how the companions dealt with their scholars. Ibn 3abbaas was the cousin of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam and had a high status, and he waited and did not knock on the door in order not to disturb the one whose knowledge he wanted to obtain.
Do that now and then, and do not go along with the behaviour, but it is important that when you make a mistake you acknowledge that you have made a mistake (such as the coming late for example) and are patient with that, so that thereby your authority is also preserved for the sake of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. The authority is also a form of awe. The authority is a form of modesty coupled with awe. That [is] the authority. Then you have authority over someone. When the modesty is removed or the awe is removed, then there is no authority anymore. The authority is not fear. The authority may not be turned into dread (coupled with fear). The dread (fear coupled with awe) is only permitted towards Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
-------------------------------------------- The end of the questions------------------------------------------------------------------------
Discussion of student 4
The sister had a case [a situation] that she also presented to the teacher about a sister who wanted to become Muslim with her. And in it she wants to connect the fourth point (the anger).
A sister became Muslim in the mosque, about whom she knew nothing beforehand. The sister became Muslim, and beforehand and afterwards she became Muslim. Afterwards she indicated that she was not convinced of Islam [not content with it]. It was said to her that it would have been better if she had remained Roman Catholic.
The sister asked the teacher's advice on this. She discussed that with the sister. She had agreed that the sister would come [to know] what Islam really is. Usually they hold a conversation with the sisters beforehand. The sister of the sister who had become Muslim would also come.
She received a message from the sister on WhatsApp and resolved not to interpret it wrongly. [The sister] indicated that Nijmegen [Nijmegen] is not next to Gouda [Gouda] and that she is busy. She is not reachable today. The sister indicated that she would not come, and that [the distance] is very far, and that she is accompanied in another place regarding Islam, and that she is not reachable by telephone.
The sister indicated that she experienced a kind of anger, and resolved to call the teacher again to present this. She felt a responsibility because she had become Muslim in the mosque of Gouda, but if she does not want to come, she does not know what she should do.
She had also received certain information about a man etc. The sister experienced anger because she did not adhere to the appointment and because she does not understand why she does not want to come while she had first indicated that she [would come].
The teacher:
As for the impulsive anger, it relates to two matters. Essentially it relates to one matter: that you become angry in a way that displeases Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. This way can be divided into a level and a method.
According to the level at which Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa wants us to become angry, we become angry, and according to the method by which we, according to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, should become angry, we should show our anger. But there is a third matter, and that is in reality also the main matter, namely the question: «Is the anger in this case the correct feeling that we should have or not?» If the answer is «yes», then what is the goal of the anger and what is the cause of the anger?
In reality, if you want to approach it in a hierarchical way, it is:
Which feeling should I have in this? The anger: yes or no? Should I become angry or should I have another feeling?
If it is yes:
What is the cause that I become angry?
What is the goal that I become angry/what do I want to reach with this?
Which level should I use in my anger?
How should I, according to the pleasure of Allaah, show my anger?
These are four questions that you should ask yourself.
Regarding this case:
We should become angry because she did not pronounce the shahaadah. How should we show our anger? We should not become angry with her, so our expression should not be towards her. We have, regarding our anger, nothing to do with her. We should show our anger towards the shaytaan. What do we show towards her? The care, and that we mention that the shaytaan has a share in this and that we make that clear.
Another sister thinks that it is a matter of ignorance and that she will not feel anger towards this woman but performs da3wah and explains more matters.
The teacher: The first question: should we become angry or should we have another feeling?
The answer to that is that we can become angry, and besides that we should also have a feeling of disappointment/sadness. Anger with sadness.
Why should we become angry and why [should we be] sad?
That we become angry because various matters went wrong:
The pushing towards the shahaadah proceeded too quickly without a conversation preceding it.
The shahaadah was forced upon [her] in a large crowd and there was continuous insistence. The imam kept saying: «Has the shahaadah been pronounced now/hurry up, etc.». In this we should become angry because Allaah does not love this. The pushing and the pressure and the influencing of the pronouncing of the shahaadah does not proceed here in complete freedom. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «لا إكراهَ في الدِّين». («There is no compulsion in the religion».) Whether it is compulsion from a large crowd, [or] pushing by blackmail, in all cases it is compulsion and the shahaadah is no longer valid when the person is no longer convinced of it. And the anger should also [be directed] at the way in which [the matter] proceeded/was pushed.
The shaytaan — the human and the djinn — distracted this sister from the religion, instead of this so-called Muslim motivating her to remain precisely in Islam. About all of this we should become angry.
We should not become angry because this woman did not adhere to her appointments. That is none of our concern at that moment. That is the last thing you should worry about. That is impulsive anger, because such anger has absolutely no value with Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
That [has] the lowest level; the entering [into Islam] has the highest level. The certainty and the da3wah have the highest level. We only obstruct ourselves in that we take into account personal matters more than [the question of] whether she enters Islam or not. The keeping of appointments or not, the caller (daa3iyah) should not become angry about it.
Some people go further in that and say «you are late, and therefore I will not help you». The impulsiveness lies in the anger because she did not adhere to her appointments, because we become angry about matters that have no priority.
Why [should we be] sad?
Because this lady was — to a certain extent — not steadfast in the entering of Islam. And because we have been sent as merciful callers. The people who perform the da3wah should be heirs of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam. And he sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam was sent as a mercy for the people. She wants to become Muslim, and because she did not become Muslim, [you have] remained sad. Aboe Hurayrah went crying to the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam because his mother had not entered Islam, when his mother insulted the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam every time he spoke about Islam. And he asked the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam to supplicate to Allaah that He guide her to Islam. If you drive your feeling well, then your feeling will push/drive you in the correct direction. And if you do not drive your feeling well, then your feeling will drive you to a wrong path.
The goal is the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, that we drive ourselves and her and those who have a connection with that towards the pleasure of Allaah.
The work towards the leadership [the responsible ones] is that this case be presented to them and that they draw a lesson from it, namely that there be no more pushing. And the second is that the shahaadah not be pronounced amidst a large crowd of people under great pressure, but that [it can be] between two or three persons.
Regarding the leadership we can learn that their happiness that someone pronounces the shahaadah [should] not drive the responsible one to have the shahaadah pronounced.
The sisters who helped: when you see in such a case such pressure and such great pushing, that you remain calm and say to the other sister who accompanies her that she says: «You do not have to feel pushed, take your time». She does not necessarily have to pronounce the shahaadah in the presence of such a large crowd.
Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says in Soerat al-3asr: «وتَواصَوا بالحَقِّ وتَواصَوا بالصَّبر». («And enjoin one another to the truth and enjoin one another to patience».)
The sister of our lessons can learn that the shahaadah should never be pronounced in such a way. Beforehand you should explain Islam (it does not have to be half an hour but it can also be five minutes), and if he wants to pronounce the shahaadah, then that can be done without pushing and without this large crowd.
Nothing will happen until we know with certainty that this person wants to enter Islam with complete freedom and with complete fundamental knowledge. We have here these basic principles.
The sadness should lead us to the supplication, that we supplicate for her that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa guides her with certainty and steadfastness to Islam and that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also guides her daughter to Islam. So you see that the anger led us to the improvement towards the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and that the sadness led to us feeling mercy for this person, in that supplication is made for her.
Regarding the woman herself you can supplicate for her and for her daughter, and that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa also guides the people who will accompany her, and that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa guides her to the correct accompaniers. That is a comprehensive supplication. And among what you can also say to her: «We know an organisation that can explain the matters well to you, and which is prepared to meet you (the organisation al-Istiqaamah). Perhaps you contact them, then you know for certain that you are accompanied by the correct people». If that [person] indicates «I do not want you to accompany me», then that is her choice.
Follow-up question: The family with whom she stayed keeps asking for a certificate [a document]. The certificate is temporarily not given. They keep asking for that certificate somewhat with the father of the sister who follows the lessons here.
They should make clear: we have received signals from this lady that she is not convinced of her Islam. As long as we are not convinced that she wants to enter Islam with certainty, we cannot give her the certificate.
Question 1:
A sister has a question in which there is also a situation with a sister [who] pronounced her shahaadah last week. She had pronounced her shahaadah (known to the sister for a longer time), and she is in the group of the al-Istiqaamah application for converts. Another sister called her, and during that call she pronounced her shahaadah directly. That was good news. The following day she wrote on the application that she is afraid, and that she will go hungry, etc. The sister then indicated that you should do it for the sake of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and that you will notice that you will no longer experience hardship. The following day she went to fast and she had not prepared herself for that. The sister wrote to her how it was going, and then it turned out that at nine o'clock in the morning she had already broken her fast. She said that she was so thirsty that she went and broke her fast.
She received afterwards from three sides a reaction that that is not correct. What exactly was further said, the sister does not know. At the end of the day she wrote to her again, whereupon the answer came: «I should not have pronounced my shahaadah but I should have done that after Ramadaan; now I suddenly feel as though everything is obligatory; before I became Muslim, I always got peace from Islam and now I do not, because now suddenly everything is [obligatory] and I feel hunted».
The answer: In this case she is Muslim, only the shaytaan is playing with her. It is important how great it is that she has entered Islam. Her feeling of being hunted is a healthy matter, because it means that she should distance herself from the Fire towards the Paradise that reaches out a hand to her. Such feelings should in reality be accompanied by a kind of accompanying text. It may not be said «no, you should not feel hunted».
Islam is obligations, but only what is good for you, and if you do not perform them, it is because they cause you harm. It will be good if the sister Haliemah speaks with her and calls her, or that the converted sister in the presence of the sister Haliemah speaks with the teacher — for example — in a group call.
The sister: The sister made contact to choose to return a little to the Tawhied. She spoke with her about the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. She added the lesson of the girls' evening that was also about that. Why should we do this? Because this is good for us. That fell well because it was a kind of reassurance. She indicated that she should have called the teacher. She made contact with Aboe Rumaysah and spoke with him. She indicated that she said that she felt a great guilt because she did not fast. [It was said to her]: it is good that you have that feeling, because it keeps you away from the Fire. Indeed, it is good that you pronounced the shahaadah, even if you experienced the feeling that everything suddenly [is obligatory]. That you pronounced the shahaadah is pure good, and do not forget that Allaah decreed that.
All of this she received very well, she noticed that there [was] a reassurance, and the fasting nevertheless remained a [difficult] step.
The teacher: That she did or did not take it up [the fasting], that is better than that she leaves the religion.
That [the matter] was brought back to the Tawhied is a good deed. And among what is important in this, [is that] among the greatest calamities and the hideous upbringing that we experience here in the Netherlands, [is] that the person, when he feels something in his heart that he does not find agreeable, distances himself at that moment from this matter.
This is 100% driving by the whim. If someone is his whole life accustomed to being driven by the whim, then the most hideous matter (there is no more hideous matter [than it]) is that you say «I do not feel comfortable with that, and if I do not feel comfortable with that, then I cannot do it». This leads the person to the Fire.
That means that at the shahaadah we should have an important share in the admonition, in that we make clear to the one who wants to pronounce the shahaadah that the fact that you become Muslim means that you surrender yourself to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. You will no longer determine your life, Allaah will determine your life. He will determine what you should find agreeable. That is when you say that there is no god but Allaah. When this [meaning] is not clear with this convert, then he has not converted [not become Muslim].
A sister called the teacher and said: «I have become Muslim, but I do not feel comfortable in the prayer, and therefore I have chosen not to pray».
The most hideous sentence [is] «I have made a considered decision not to pray, because I do not feel comfortable with that». The teacher asked her: «Why did you become Muslim?» She said: «I became Muslim because I felt comfortable with it, because it agreed with my feeling, and the prayer does not agree with my feeling». O sister, said the teacher, then you were never Muslim, because you surrender yourself to Allaah, and He determines as God what you find agreeable and what you do not find agreeable, and what you should do and what you should not do.
That [is] Islam, and we should not be frightened of it. This is the core of Islam. If the person does not believe in that, then he is not a Muslim and cannot become a Muslim. This is an extremely important matter that should be taken up with the converts. And especially the young converts, because they have often learned at school «do what you feel comfortable with, and if something does not make you happy, then do not do it». This is the upbringing that is given today at school. Therefore we should place an extra emphasis on this with the converts.
The next lesson
Today we did not learn new characteristics. Next week we continue the rest of the characteristics of the educator. And in shaa-a Allaah many more matters will then be raised regarding matters that we should improve or work on.
The homework
Organise your notes and study them for at least two hours.
Check at each characteristic that we dealt with which matters you should improve in it and write that down. Then we discuss that next week, in shaa-a Allaah.
Begin from now with at least five of these ten characteristics to improve yourself.
Lesson fifty-six — Sunday 16 June 2019
The homework
Organise your notes.
Check at each characteristic that we dealt with which matters you should improve in it and write that down. Then we discuss that next week, in shaa-a Allaah.
Begin from now with at least five of these ten characteristics to improve yourself.
Next week we begin — in shaa-a Allaah — with the eleventh characteristic of the educator. After the characteristics of the educator we will deal with the domains, in shaa-a Allaah.
Discussion of the homework (16 June 2019)
Discussion of student 1
The first time that the sister did the assignment, she had nevertheless done it in a not entirely correct way. The image that the sister had about her parents regarding their position towards her was not entirely correct.
She chose the characteristic of al-hilm and al-anaah. That means patience coupled with the use of caution and intellect. She did not yet deal with it in the correct way and she wanted to try to bring about a change in that.
And besides that she chose that the admonition is not continuous. There should be a time space between the different admonitions so that the person does not become bored. There should be more quality than quantity. With this the sister engaged consciously. She is in her environment with a converted sister who became Muslim about three years ago; she also notices in her, in her manners and her behaviour, that she falls short much in that and that much of her old upbringing, that whole Dutch character, is still in her. She tries to advise her to gather knowledge. For a time that was bothersome to the converted sister if she said even a small thing as a reminder. Now the sister engaged with that in a different way. She chose to leave a time space, but in a different way. For example: soon a course begins for converts and interested people. «If you like, you can also register, we can go together by car, you get to know many more people», etc. The sister notices that [the matter] then falls better, although the sister says that she has no time and/or that she has to work, but without there being [any] enmity. The sister sees that as a step closer towards the gathering of knowledge.
And besides that she chose to be a good example. To not be disobedient to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. That was also with a sister whom she knows well. They sat together in the car and went to the lesson, but they were a little tired. Thus their conversation also began that they had not slept well and such matters. Then the sister said: no, we will not be negative today but we will be positive today. Instead of enumerating how tired they were, [they went] mentioning the blessings, that they had nevertheless been able to sleep a little, and that they would continue the lessons, and that they had overcome the shaytaan. At a certain moment the other sister went along in that until they both affirmed positive matters.
There is [between her] and those sisters no educational bond, but they are matters that she brought up regarding the assignment and what she did with it.
Discussion of student 2
She dealt with the second characteristic (the care and the softness). She cannot distinguish well between the fitrah characteristics [and the personality characteristics], and she asks whether the care belongs to the fitrah characteristics.
The teacher: The care does not belong to the fitrah characteristics but is something that you acquire.
The sister: In the softness the sister sometimes exaggerates, so that it is difficult for her to set limits with others. She quickly tends to think «it is just a child», for example in theft. That is a trap in which she is continuously caught.
The teacher: That is not excess in the softness, that is a form of neglecting the responsibility. The problem is that when you classify it under the softness, you will not solve it, you will not correct it but will do the opposite of what is required, so that you become harsher and think that you can solve it. When you classify it under the correct designation (the neglect), then you will be more alert in your feeling. When your child does something like this, if it were big/a teenager, which ruling would such behaviour get (sin, no sin, great sin), according to that ruling you should behave in an educational way, because the upbringing of the child is a preparation for its buloegh, so that it is prepared to bear its responsibility regarding its deeds and words. That means that her feeling regarding its deed or word may not be disdainful or negligent. The loyalty to Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa should be good to such an extent that you also treat the deed according to what the ruling of the deed is.
An example of that is that a child — for example — takes candy without permission. If it were a little older, that would be called theft. Thus you should call it in your heart. A child that hits a parent, it would be a great sin if it grew up. A child that does not tell the truth and makes a joke of it, what would that be called if it grew up, and so forth.
Thereby you prepare it, otherwise that [person] is so heedless that he is in reality bringing up a backbiter, a thief, a deceiver, a liar, under the pretext of the comfort «ah, it is still small».
The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam was sitting with 3abdullaah ibn 3abbaas [3umar ibn Abie Salamah] at the table and saw his hand roaming in the dish. Then he said to him: «يا غُلام، سَمِّ الله، وكُل بيمينك، وكُل مما يَليك». («O boy, mention the Name of Allaah, and eat with your right hand, and eat from what is nearest to you».) If [the matter] relates to such behavioural manners that are obligatory, then the leaving of these matters is small. But regarding the great sins, then you should point them out to him even more and make them detestable to him.
The child, thereby you form its 3aqiedah. What does the 3aqiedah mean exactly? Some people think directly of the Tawhied of the worship-worthiness (uloehiyyah), the names and attributes, and the lordship (ruboebiyyah), but that is not complete. You form its love and its hatred and the way in which it loves and hates. You determine for it the source, what it should love and how it should do that, and what it should hate and how it does that. That [is] the core of the 3aqiedah with which it moves.
If you do not do that [it is] as comfort for yourself or heedlessness. If you do not do that, then you give a counterproductive upbringing.
When you connect the problem to an incorrect cause, then you will not find the solution and you will enlarge the problem or precisely add an additional problem.
The sister: At the fourth characteristic (the controlling of the anger) the sister caught herself that when she becomes angry, she becomes angry about personal matters and not about what Allaah or the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam becomes angry about.
The teacher: How did you improve that?
The sister: At the anger I looked whether Allaah becomes angry about this.
The teacher: Can you give an example of this?
The sister: More personal annoyances because of — for example — an annoyed face. More annoyances provoke my anger. She calms herself by knowing why I become angry about this, what are my priorities? Let us suppose that an Islamic matter is violated, then the sister tends to seek an excuse for that [person].
Example: suppose that someone does not wear the headscarf: she tries to invent excuses why the sister does not wear the headscarf. And she exaggerates in that to such an extent that she sees it as a smaller matter.
That relates to the anger, because she does not want to keep the anger in the heart, whereas in reality she should want to keep the anger in her heart, but she tries to calm herself. Her scale is not correct according to the sister.
The teacher: This is not a good assumption, [nor] a good reasoning whether [the matter] is correct or not. In reality you should ask yourself: do I prefer to advise her or not? Is [the matter] that I find a great obstacle to advise, or is there another matter?
The sister: Perhaps the first matter is that I exaggerate in that, so that she neglects her responsibility to give advice.
The teacher: Your companion (your companion [of the djinn]) knows your whims and lets you comfort yourself so that you do not move on to the advice. This too is not a good assumption. The correct thing is that you think «this sister would like to be advised and I will advise her in order to turn her away from the Fire and the curse in which she finds herself». A good assumption is only something that brings you closer towards the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, not something that distances you from the pleasure of Allaah.
When you go and invent all the excuses to justify the non-wearing of the headscarf or to comfort [with it], then it means in reality that you are saying that Allaah did not prepare her for that, that she does not know whether she wears the headscarf, [that] if I advise her, she will become angrier.
Who commanded that advice be given? Allaah. And He is the One whose heart is in His hand.
The good assumption about the people is built on the good assumption about Allaah and depends on it and is according to it. Then you know that Allaah will guide you, and you do this with the knowledge that you have got, Allaah will help you, that certainty you have. This good assumption about Allaah will lead you to think that her heart is in the hand of Allaah when He knows that she wants the good.
The good assumption about the people depends on the good assumption about Allaah and is connected to it. This may never be forgotten. It is never ever permitted for you to disdain a sin, or to neglect it, or to leave it [to persist].
The sins you treat according to the way of the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam; sometimes he teaches us to act directly, and sometimes to confront, that is according to the situation.
We have also dealt before with the methods of the admonition. And we have also dealt before with the advice, when you give an open advice, and a private advice, when [it is] on the covering, you have several forms of the covering.
The Sunnah teaches us how we should deal with that, not our whims. If you make a mistake in the estimation of the Sunnah, then that is better than that you think that you have done well. A mistake on a good basis is better than a good deed built on a bad basis. The good deed built on a bad basis is bad in any case.
Do you get a reward for the thoughts that are built on your whims? No. Even if you would according to the Sunnah act in a good way. But when your thoughts were built on your whims, then you get no reward and you have not done what pleases Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
When your consideration is the Sunnah, then at that moment, despite that you have made a mistake, you will get a reward for your mistake, because you have competed to obtain the good, to follow the Sunnah.
With the scholars of the companions they did not call [the matter] fiqh [understanding] except when that person also practises the knowledge. The person does not have fiqh except when they know how they should carry it out practically. Therefore some of them have more knowledge than others, because that [person] with less information at least practises that knowledge, and whoever has more knowledge [but] does not practise the knowledge, therefore has less knowledge.
The sister: The seventh characteristic (the learning of what the moderation is) the sister still has, but she had dealt with it in the previous lesson.
Discussion of student 3

chapters.title: ٢. حَسِّن نفسَك بوصفك مُرَبِّيًا

sections.content:
- التربيةُ الصحيحةُ تبدأ من نفسك.

تَظُنُّ خاصَّةً أنَّها بمُتابَعةِ الدروسِ ودراساتِ الإسلامِ تَعمَلُ على نفسها.

- تَعَرَّف على نجاحاتِ التربيةِ القائمةِ والصحيحة

كان عند الأختِ هنا العكسُ. لم تَكُن قد التَقَتْ بناسٍ عندهم نجاحاتُ تربيةٍ صحيحة. كان عندها خاصَّةً في تربيتها هي أنَّها تحدَّثَتْ مع أُمِّها كيف كانت تربيتُها وأنَّها غيرُ صحيحةٍ البتَّةَ وأنَّها لا ينبغي أن تَفعَلَ ذلك. تناولَتِ التربيةَ غيرَ الصحيحةِ حتى تَعرِفَ ما لا ينبغي أن تَفعَلَه.

- اعرِفِ العَوائقَ في التربية

الإخلاصُ كان في غايةِ الأهميَّةِ في هذا. تُلاحِظُ في نفسها في [مجالِ] العملِ الإغاثيِّ [hulpverlening] أنَّ الإخلاصَ في غايةِ الأهميَّةِ وأنَّها أحيانًا ينبغي أن تَعمَلَ عليه. ينبغي أن تكون واعيةً أنَّها ينبغي أن تُوقِظَ الإخلاصَ كلَّ مرَّةٍ من جديد (لماذا تَفعَلينَ هذا، فقط لأجلِ ثوابِ الله سبحانه وتعالى)، وذلك أيضًا النقطةُ التالية، أنَّ النتيجةَ إلى الله وحدَه.

- عندك إخلاصٌ وتَفعَلُ ما ينبغي أن تَفعَلَه وينبغي أن تَصبِرَ في ذلك. الخيرُ والشَّرُّ كلاهما ابتلاء.

هاتانِ نقطتانِ ينبغي أن تَبقى تُكَرِّرُهما لنفسها (الإخلاصُ، وألَّا تَتوقَّعَ أنَّ النتيجةَ ستأتي كلَّها حَسَنةً ودَفعةً واحدةً، وأنَّها ينبغي أن يكون عندها صبرٌ أكثر).

مناقشةُ طالبةٍ ٢

أَبدَتِ الأختُ أنَّها تحدَّثَتْ مع أختٍ لتُناقِشَ نجاحاتِ التربية. ستَتَّصِلُ بها عمَّا قريبٍ في ذلك.

فيما يَخُصُّ السُّنَنَ الكَونيَّةَ التي ذُكِرَت في الدرسِ الماضي (مرارًا) أَعطَتْها الأختُ لونًا مُستَقِلًّا حتى تستطيعَ فيما بعدُ أن تَستَخرِجَها من كلِّ الملاحظات.

وفي الباقي عَمِلَتْها على النحوِ نفسِه الذي عَمِلَتْها به الأختُ التي ناقَشَتِ الواجبَ للتوّ.
لتُؤَسِّسَ تربيةً وتُهَيِّئَها على وجهٍ صحيحٍ من المهمِّ أن تُؤَسِّسَ/تأخذَ النقاطَ التالية.

٨. كلُّ مُرَبٍّ ينبغي أن يَعلَمَ أنَّه في تربيته ينبغي أن يُراعيَ اختلافَ مرحلةِ التربيةِ وأن يُفَرِّقَ فيها بحسبِ مرحلةِ حياةِ الولد.

الولدُ له/يَعرِفُ عِدَّةَ مراحلَ عُمُريَّةٍ، وكلُّ مرحلةٍ عُمُريَّةٍ لها صفاتُها الخاصَّة.
sections.content_nl:
Ik ben sinds de vorige les mij ervan bewust geworden dat de barmhartigheid gebouwd behoort te zijn op de liefde en genegenheid voor het kind, gekoppeld aan de wetgevingen van Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa (verheven en geprezen is Hij).
Barmhartigheid is dat je met het kind omgaat op een wijze waardoor het wordt opgevoed naar de goede eigenschappen.
Welke zaken behoor ik hierin te verbeteren?
Dat ik de juiste ervaring verwerf in welke situaties — volgens de wetgevingen van Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa — liefde, troost, omhelzing en warmte belangrijk zijn als een vorm van barmhartigheid, en in welke situaties strengheid en hardheid belangrijk zijn als een vorm van barmhartigheid.
Het is in beide gevallen belangrijk — hardheid of zachtheid jegens het kind — dat ik duidelijk maak dat ik hard/zacht met hem ben omwille van Allaah.
En ook behoor ik meer kennis te verzamelen over hoe ik barmhartig ben met mijn kinderen, om te weten of ik barmhartig ben volgens de wetgevingen van Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa dan wel volgens mijn eigen begeerte of de begeerte van mijn kinderen.
Wat heb ik gedaan?
Ik heb mijn neefje (dat geen Muslim is) bij het kopen van cadeaus aangesproken dat hij blij behoort te zijn met één product en niet onachtzaam [nalatig] mag zijn, omdat Allaah dat niet liefheeft. Ik heb mijn neefje over Allaah verteld. Dat Hij het is Die erop toeziet dat mijn neefje zijn cadeaus krijgt, omdat Hij papa en mama geld geeft. De zuster doet dit vaak zonder dat de moeder van het kind aanwezig is. Soms komt bij de zuster de gedachte op dat het niet veel uithaalt omdat zijn ouders geen Muslims zijn, en dat zodra hij thuiskomt [de zaak] bedorven [verpest] kan worden.
De ustaadh (de leraar): Laten we aannemen dat jouw redenering juist is, dan betekent dat niet dat je niet zou moeten proberen. Jouw redenering staat 180 graden op zijn kop. En dat betekent dat jouw redenering, als je haar zou omkeren, pas dán juist zou zijn, want wanneer je een kind aanspreekt, spreek je de fitrah (natuurlijke aanleg) aan en spreek je het als een Muslim aan. Je spreekt zijn fitrah aan die overeenstemt met de Tawhied (de Eenheid van Allaah) waartoe jij oproept. Het kind kan je met deze woorden die je gezegd hebt, vanaf de leeftijd van twee jaar begrijpen, vanaf anderhalf jaar kan het je begrijpen, alleen kan het nog niets terugzeggen. Hoe vaker je dat herhaalt, hoe beter het dat begrijpt.
Er werd [eens] een straat-da3wah (oproep tot de Islam) verricht, en tijdens de training zei de ustaadh tegen de broeders en zusters: wanneer jullie niet de gelovigen aanspreken, weet dan dat jullie hun kinderen aanspreken voordat jullie hén aanspreken. Wees in jullie woorden heel eenvoudig, want jullie spreken dan de fitrah van de kinderen aan. Het is belangrijk dat jullie dat in jullie hoofd bewaren en de shaytaan (de duivel) jullie niet laten ontmoedigen. Al die [andere zaken] zijn middelen waarmee hij de da3wah niet zal begrijpen.
Je hebt je best gedaan om hem te leiden en Allaah tevreden te stellen. Je behoort het te doen omwille van de beloning. Wanneer dat jouw intentie is, dan is het onmogelijk dat de shaytaan je ontmoedigt. Allaah leidt hem. Waar het om gaat is dat jij jouw beloning wilt. De shaytaan kan hierin sluw zijn, dus behoren wij nog sluwer en slimmer te zijn door ons enkel te houden aan de eenvoudige basisregels waarmee wij Allaah tevreden kunnen stellen. De ikhlaas (oprechtheid) is heel eenvoudig, maar als je haar gaat toepassen, vergt zij concentratie en bewustzijn.
Je kunt eenvoudigweg zeggen: Allaah bestaat, Allaah heeft ons allen geschapen. Hij heeft papa geschapen en Hij heeft mama geschapen. [Het is] heel eenvoudig.
Eigenlijk zijn er [daar] voor dit vier stappen:
Dat je spreekt over het bestaan van Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa en wie Allaah is, Zijn Namen en Eigenschappen en dat Hij geweldig is.
Wat Hij heeft gedaan en wat Hij doet (dat Hij alles bestuurt en dat Hij alles heeft geschapen). Dat je zegt: Allaah heeft je dat gegeven. Heb je gezegd: o Allaah, dank U? Omdat Allaah je papa of je mama geld heeft gegeven.
Dat je hem Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa laat aanbidden door hem te laten danken, en door hem meer te vertellen over Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, en de Profeet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam (Allaahs vrede en zegeningen zij met hem), en dat Allaah hem heeft gebracht om Allaah te aanbidden.
Ken je het verhaal van het kind (het meisje Anouk)?
Deze Anouk kwam voort uit een verslaafde vader en moeder (die injecteren, drinken, inhaleren en pillen nemen). Zij hebben geen onderdak. Zij is nu op dit moment ongeveer acht/negen jaar oud, zij bidt en draagt de volledige khimaar (hoofdbedekking), en door middel van haar heeft Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa ook haar familie praktiserend gemaakt. Begrijpt zo'n kind je? Ja.
Misschien begrijpt de ouder minder dan het kind.
sections.title_nl: 3. De barmhartigheid
sections.content_en:
Since the previous lesson I have become aware that mercy ought to be built upon love and affection for the child, coupled with the legislations of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa (glorified and exalted is He).
Mercy is that you deal with the child in a manner by which he is raised toward the good characteristics.
Which matters ought I to improve in this?
That I acquire the correct experience as to in which situations — according to the legislations of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa — love, consolation, embracing and warmth are important as a form of mercy, and in which situations firmness and harshness are important as a form of mercy.
It is important in both cases — harshness or gentleness toward the child — that I make clear that I am harsh/gentle with him for the sake of Allaah.
And also I ought to gather more knowledge about how I am to be merciful with my children, in order to know whether I am merciful according to the legislations of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa or according to my own desire or the desire of my children.
What did I do?
I addressed my nephew (who is not a Muslim), when buying gifts, [saying] that he ought to be happy with one product and not be heedless [negligent], because Allaah does not love that. I told my nephew about Allaah. That He is the One Who ensures that my nephew receives his gifts, because He gives papa and mama money. The sister often does this without the child's mother being present. Sometimes the thought comes to the sister that it does not help much because his parents are not Muslims, and that as soon as he returns home [the matter] may be spoiled [ruined].
The ustaadh (the teacher): Let us suppose that your reasoning is correct; that does not mean that you ought not to try. Your reasoning is turned 180 degrees upside down. And that means that your reasoning, if you were to reverse it, would only then be correct, because when you address a child you are addressing the fitrah (natural disposition), so you address him as a Muslim. You address his fitrah, which is in agreement with the Tawhied (the Oneness of Allaah) to which you call. The child, with these words that you have said, can understand you from the age of two years; from one and a half years he can understand you, except that he cannot say anything back. The more you repeat that, the better he understands it.
A street da3wah (call to Islam) was once carried out, and during the training the ustaadh said to the brothers and sisters: when you are not addressing the believers, know that you are addressing their children before you address them. Be very simple in your words, because you are then addressing the fitrah of the children. It is important that you keep that in your heads and not let the shaytaan (the devil) discourage you. All those [other things] are means by which he will not understand the da3wah.
You exerted the effort to guide him and to please Allaah. You ought to do it for the sake of the reward. When that is your intention, then it is impossible for the shaytaan to discourage you. Allaah guides him. The point is that you want your reward. The shaytaan can be cunning in this, so we ought to be even more cunning and clever by adhering only to the simple basic rules by which we can please Allaah. Ikhlaas (sincerity) is very simple, but if you go to practice it, it requires concentration and awareness.
You can simply say: Allaah exists, Allaah created us all. He created papa and He created mama. [It is] very simple.
Essentially [there] are four steps for this:
That you speak about the existence of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and who Allaah is, His Names and Attributes and that He is magnificent.
What He has done and what He does (that He governs everything and that He created everything). That you say: Allaah gave you that. Did you say: O Allaah, thank You? Because Allaah gave your papa or your mama money.
That you make him worship Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa by making him give thanks, and by telling him more about Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa, and the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam (may Allaah's peace and blessings be upon him), and that Allaah brought him [into being] to worship Allaah.
Do you know the story of the child (the girl Anouk)?
This Anouk came from an addicted father and mother (who inject, drink, inhale, and take pills). They have no shelter. She is now, at this moment, about eight/nine years old; she prays and wears the full khimaar (headcovering), and through her Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa has also made her family practicing. Does such a child understand you? Yes.
Perhaps the parent understands less than the child.
